newsitem.title: JAPAN: Deadly influenza virus hits Japan's elderly.
newsitem.headline: Deadly influenza virus hits Japan's elderly.

text.p: An influenza virus that has killed nearly 80 people in the past month threatens to sweep through the homes of the elderly in Japan, a Health Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The seasonal rise in flu cases in late December, was the highest on record... We are expecting many deaths, particularly amongst the elderly," the health official told Reuters.

Health authorities in Iwate Prefecture, hardest hit by the flu epidemic with 20 deaths of residents of homes for the elderly since the end of December, say the virus kills with alarming speed, the official said.
"It can take only two days in some cases for the first signs of fever to turn into death by pneumonia... Some of the victims don't even get the fever," he said.
Prefectural authorities have alerted nursing homes and health workers, instructing them to carry out preventive measures to slow the spread of the virus.

"We have told them to be on the lookout for the first signs of a cold and to separate off those who appear to have a cold so the other residents will have a better chance of not being infected," he said.
Local health authorities in six prefectures have reported 76 deaths this year due to the "Hong Kong A" virus, which originated in Hong Kong two years ago and spread to Russia last year.
A Health Ministry official said he expected large numbers of deaths this winter due to the Hong Kong A virus.
